solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: French author passing around quiet university grounds

indicators.note: the author's name is wrapped around the next piece, as if passing round it

parts.note: Albert Camus, French author of The Outsider
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A French writer strolls round a hushed university's grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing around' puts P inside CAMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the site and buildings of a university or college.

indicators.note: awfully suggests the name has been badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shane is looking terribly pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone ashen-faced has gone the grey colour of ash, very pale.

indicators.note: gathered says the letters of the words are collected up together in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener says: I gathered a peanut plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' is the anagram signal on PEANUT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the petunia is a common garden plant with trumpet-shaped flowers.

indicators.note: lacking says the country's name goes without the following word

explanation.surface: A nation said to be short of natural springs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes IN from SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a spa is a mineral spring, or a resort built around one.

definitions.meaning: an electronic dance music style from the 1990s
as a verb: to store a car under cover

explanation.surface: A dance music style linked to house music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'house' as another dance genre; in fact it is the verb, to keep a car under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage is a dance music style, and to garage a car is to shelter it, to house it.

explanation.surface: Walk off, take the fruit, and lose your temper!
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go bananas is to become wildly angry or crazed.

indicators.note: did you say asks us to hear the word rather than read it

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a lift is held up by beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did you say' signals RAYS sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lift something is to raise it.

clue.text: Horse laid up, hurt — sweet thing

indicators.note: in a down clue, laid up means written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A horse is laid up and in pain: it is a sweet thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' turns NAG into GAN, read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganache is a rich chocolate and cream filling, a confection or sweet item.

clue.text: A hit with bean curd, a strange meat dish

indicators.note: strange says these letters come out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Bean curd as a hit dish: a strange idea for a meat course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges A HIT BEAN CURD A; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: chateaubriand is a thick cut of beef fillet, a classic meat dish.

indicators.note: not starting says the word for rule loses its first letter

parts.note: a canon is a rule or law, as in church canon

explanation.surface: A rule is not starting any time soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops C from CANON.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word meaning shortly, in a little while.

parts.note: time is a prison term, and a judge passes it on the convicted, so it is time passed rather than time that passes

explanation.surface: Time that simply goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: Time 'passes' by itself; here a judge does the passing, of a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term served is called time, and judges pass this punishment on offenders.

indicators.note: ruined says the word is wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A nasty person, thin, spoiled the label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges LABEL to EBALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimeball is slang for a repellent, untrustworthy person.

indicators.note: accommodating says the nation holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Mali is a West African nation

explanation.surface: A country takes in a western nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts A and W inside MALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a country in south-east Africa.

parts.note: a successful business is said to take off; this firm's planes literally take off

explanation.surface: A company that becomes a sudden success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes off' reads as booming trade; here it is aircraft leaving the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier company that flies passengers is a business whose aircraft take off.

definitions.meaning: one is an example of a figure such as seven or ten
more deadened or desensitised, the comparative of numb

explanation.surface: A single person who has become less sensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer two ways: NUMBER as a figure, and NUMB-ER, more numb.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an example of a figure; more numb means having less feeling.

indicators.note: docked means having the tail cut off, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An island where a large cat has had its tail cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' takes T off CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

definitions.meaning: thin dry savoury biscuits, often eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: A snack of nuts and biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like food beside biscuits, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers means mad, as nuts does, and crackers are crisp savoury biscuits.

clue.text: Coming up in winter, a deciduous tree

indicators.note: Coming up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deciduous tree comes up in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the hiding signal, added to the draft, which left it as a link word. 'Coming up' reverses RADEC in this down light. The surface misleads: the answer is evergreen, not deciduous.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the cedar is a large evergreen conifer.

definitions.meaning: to raise, as a car with a hand tool
the knave in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Pick up a card.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack up is to lift a car, and the jack is the playing card below the queen.

clue.text: Gateaux, last of those in different sack

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
different says the word is made into a different arrangement of its letters
last of picks only the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Gateaux, the last of them, put in a different sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges SACK to CAKS; 'in' puts E, from 'last of those', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateaux are rich layered cream sponge cakes.

definitions.meaning: an unofficial walkout by workers called at short notice
a lion is a wild cat, and an attack is a strike

explanation.surface: A lion's sudden pounce.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildcat strike is an abrupt unofficial stoppage; a big cat's assault is jokingly the same thing.

indicators.note: Into says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A healthy woman who is into keeping fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' reads as keen on, but it signals the letters lying inside 'fitness, healthy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for a female person stands in for a woman.

indicators.note: spoken of says the word for fuel is heard, not seen

parts.note: petrol is the British word for car fuel, gasoline

explanation.surface: Fuel mentioned for an aircraft pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken of' signals PETROL (British for gasoline) sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the petrel is a seabird, so a flier.

clue.text: Pass by eastern part of church behind back of chancel

indicators.note: behind says the church part comes after the letter before it
back of picks out the final letter of the word

parts.note: the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: Walk past the eastern end of a church, behind the chancel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of chancel' gives L; 'behind' places APSE after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: when time passes by, it is said to elapse.
